chats.answer:
The best HDMI extender splitter depends on whether you want to send one HDMI signal to multiple TVs over long distances or simply duplicate it to nearby displays.

For most home and commercial installations, I'd recommend a 4K HDMI-over-Cat6 splitter/extender. It uses Ethernet-style cables to distribute one video source to multiple displays.

Here's what to look for:

4K @ 60Hz support, preferably with HDR.

1-in-2 or 1-in-4 outputs, depending on how many TVs you have.

Cat6 transmission for runs of 50–100 meters.

PoC (Power over Cable) to reduce the number of power adapters.

EDID management to avoid resolution and compatibility problems.

chats.answer:
The best HDMI extender splitter depends on whether you want to send one HDMI source to multiple TVs over long distances or simply duplicate the signal to nearby displays.

For most setups with multiple TVs in different rooms, I recommend a 1-in-4-out HDMI splitter extender over Cat6 Ethernet cable, ideally supporting 4K@60Hz, HDR, EDID management, and IR remote control.

What to look for

Recommendation

Outputs

Cat6 HDMI extender kit




HDR

	

HDR10 support




Remote control

	

IR passthrough




Compatibility

	

HDCP 2.2/2.3 and EDID management

Important: An HDMI splitter duplicates the same picture across all TVs. If you want different content on different TVs, you need an HDMI matrix instead.
